key_insight: A feedforward neural network using the writhe density matrix can classify the first six prime two-component links with high accuracy, showing topology information is learnable from geometric descriptors.
engineering_relevance: This offers a fast surrogate for link-topology identification in polymer, DNA, and protein systems where exact invariant calculations are too costly for large-scale simulations.
method: Build writhe density matrix features from equilibrated link configurations.
Train a feedforward neural network to predict link class.
Test robustness across temperature, component length, and added Gaussian noise.
evidence_signal: The model achieves 97% accuracy on thermally equilibrated configurations and remains strong across temperatures and lengths, but degrades quickly under topology-altering Gaussian noise.
watch_item: Performance may not transfer reliably when the input geometry is perturbed in ways that alter topology, so careful validation is needed before use on noisy or underresolved data.
paper_title: Writhe-Based Polymer Link Classification Using Machine Learning
